content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: chat deflection on both queues lifts predicted service level to 81.6% for 18:15-20:00 at ₹312 extra cost.","why":"The general queue is running well over forecast with no identified cause: 72 calls at 18:00 against 43.9 forecast (+64%), and +31% for the day. The rise is spread evenly across all call reasons. Staffing and handle time are on plan, so this is a demand problem. Service level fell to 51.4% at 18:00. Doing nothing is predicted to give 72.3% over 18:15-20:00, below the 80% target, with 6.5% abandons. P1 moves 20% of balance enquiries (general) and 20% of payment status enquiries (payments) to chat. That gives a predicted 81.6% overall with abandons at 4.2%. It is the cheapest plan that meets the target, and it breaks no policy.","trade_offs":["The general queue stays below target under P1 at 75.2%. Payments reaches 87.5%, and that lifts the combined figure over 80%.","P2 (₹2,250) uses overtime for 10 general agents and gets general to 91.7% and 86.3% overall. It costs about 7x more, and payments falls to 81.2%.","P4 (₹1,944) gets 88.3% overall, with general at 89.9% and abandons at 2.3%. It costs about ₹1,630 more than P1.","P3 (₹2,562) gives the strongest result: 93.8% overall and 1.3% abandons. It is the most expensive option.","P1 has almost no buffer at 81.6% against an 80% target. It also depends on customers actually accepting the move to chat."],"watch":"The cause of the surge is unknown, so check the general queue's arrivals and service level after 18:30. If general stays near 75% or volume keeps climbing, add overtime (the P4 or P2 options from 18:45). Also confirm the chat team can absorb the deflected contacts."}
